summary: Tested forgot-password flow (both on /compte and /commande) + favorites feature. Backend endpoints all pass (5/5). Frontend: /compte forgot flow works (reset-link-box, navigation to /reset-password, unknown email hidden). Favorites work end-to-end for logged-in customers (add, toast, red heart, panel display, remove, product page fav-btn). Non-connected user gets 'Connectez-vous' toast. CHECKOUT forgot-password is BROKEN due to nested <form> elements in Checkout.jsx — inner submit button submits the outer checkout form instead of doForgot handler, so the checkout-reset-link-box never appears.

ui_bugs.issue: Nested <form> tags: <form onSubmit={submit}> (line 167) wraps <form onSubmit={doForgot}> (line 177) and <form onSubmit={doQuickLogin}> (line 193). HTML disallows nested forms; browser strips inner form tags, so 'checkout-forgot-submit' and 'checkout-login-submit' buttons submit the OUTER checkout form. Result: URL changes /commande -> /commande? (native GET submit), doForgot never runs, checkout-reset-link-box never appears. Same defect will affect checkout quick-login submit. React logs hydration errors 'form cannot be a descendant of form'.

Local `favorites` state is fetched only once in useEffect on mount. Removing a favorite via heart button updates FavoritesContext.ids but NOT the Dashboard's favorites array, so the removed product remains visible until user navigates away and back. Re-clicking tab-favorites does not re-fetch (tab already active).

rca of the issue: Checkout.jsx renders <form onSubmit={submit}> as the outer order form. Inside it, at lines 177 and 193, two additional <form> elements are declared for the login/forgot quick-widgets. HTML5 spec forbids nested forms; browsers silently drop the inner form tags during parsing. Therefore any <button type='submit'> inside those pseudo-forms fires the outer form's onSubmit (or the browser's default GET submit) instead of doForgot/doQuickLogin. Observed: clicking checkout-forgot-submit navigates from /commande to /commande? (default GET) and no state update occurs. Mitigation: convert inner forms to divs and change submit buttons to type='button' invoking the handler on click; or portal the login/forgot widget outside the outer form.
